tickets.title: PIM readiness: stock, MOQ and badges behind provider interfaces
tickets.scope:
The backend plan (elme-product-data skill): no stock is stored in Magento (live from the Shipment Service), MOQ and promo prices come from the data warehouse, product fields from the PIM. Prices already sit behind `CustomerPriceProviderInterface`; do the same for the rest, with no change in behaviour today.

- Stock: one `StockProviderInterface` (label level, salable qty, available yes/no, for one SKU and for many at once). Default implementation reads Magento inventory as now. Move the four direct reads onto it: `Elme\Theme\ViewModel\ProductTile`, `Elme\Theme\ViewModel\Lookbook`, `Elme\QtyRules\Model\QtyRules`, `Elme\QuickOrder\Model\CartLines`.
- MOQ: one `QtyRulesProviderInterface` (minimum, step, maximum per SKU). Default implementation reads the Magento stock item as `QtyRules::fromStockItem` does now.
- Badges: Sale and New in `ProductTile` read `special_price` and `news_from_date` directly; put them behind one method per badge, so Sale can follow the promo price and New the launch date later.
- `bestsellers` sort attribute (patch `ConfigurePlpToolbar`): write in the ticket who fills it once the PIM owns product data, or mark it as Magento-owned.
- Grep the Elme modules and theme for any other direct read of Magento inventory or of an old attribute listed as Drop / Not PIM in `references/m2-attribute-map.csv`, and list what you find.

Do not build a client for the PIM, the data warehouse or the Shipment Service here.
qa: No class outside the two default implementations injects a Magento inventory interface (grep is clean)
Card stock label, Shop the Looks, cart availability and MOQ messages behave exactly as before
Swapping the stock provider in di.xml for a stub changes every one of the four places
Unit tests cover both default implementations and the many-SKUs call
The ticket log lists every other direct read found, or says none
